newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SBC nine-month ordinary net up 27 pct.
newsitem.headline: SBC nine-month ordinary net up 27 pct.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corporation (SBC) said third quarter results slowed and ordinary net profit after tax was up 27 percent from the same 1995 period.
An SBC statement said the total figure for depreciation and value adjustments in the third quarter continued to be high and above the average foir the previous year.
It said net operating income rose 17 percent for the first three quarters as against the same 1995 period.

"Compared with the first half of the year, growth was slower in the third quarter, reflecting lower trading volumes on the financial markets which affected trading income," SBC said. The bank said its nine-month net profit rise of 27 percent compared with an increase of 36 percent in the first six months of this year.
The statement on performance from January through to September did not provide any numbers for the individual results.
Although trading income slowed in the third quarter, SBC said the nine-month total was nearly as high as for all of 1995.
"Net commission income for the first time contributed over 40 percent to operating income and continues to be by far the most important earnings component," the bank said.
Net commission income also slowed in the third quarter, but the nine-month cumulative figure was still 30 percent higher than in the same period last year.

"Net interest income remained on a similar order of magnitude as in the two previous quarters, and the cumulative result for the first nine months was higher than the comparable 1995 figure," SBC added.
It said loan loss provisions were almost exclusively related to exposure in Switzerland, where an economic recovery has been slow to materialise.
"Depreciation and value adjustments in the past three months remained at an unchanged high level," the bank added.
Personnel expenses were lower in the third quarter than in the two previous quarters, mainly due to smaller provisions for performance-related compensation.
Personnel costs therefore grew less strongly in the first nine months than in the first half when compared to last year, SBC said.
Operating expenses continued to rise gradually and were higher for the nine months than in the same 1995 period.
"The main reason for this is the implementation of various information technology projects according to plan," SBC said.
But it said administrative expenses as whole fell slightly in the third quarter.
